text:
meera: quick heads-up: after we bumped httpx to 0.24 in the sync SDK, a few services reported sudden socket churn and connection resets under steady state. suspected regression in pool defaults. anyone else?

jon: saw alerts too. tcp TIME_WAITs spiking and ephemeral port exhaustion on k8s nodes. pattern looks like connections aren't being reused; new sockets each request.

ravi: useful repro: small sync script hitting the embeddings endpoint at QPS ~120 with a single Client instance. switching to Client(pool_limits=PoolLimits(max_connections=100, max_keepalive_connections=20)) reduced churn.

meera: ok can you paste the snippet?

ravi: sure:
```py
from redwood import Client
from httpx_limits import PoolLimits  # pseudo import for example

client = Client(api_key="x", pool_limits=PoolLimits(max_connections=100, max_keepalive_connections=20))
for _ in range(10000):
    client.embeddings(["a" * 100])
```

jon: two things: 1) we currently expose pool_limits on sync client but not on AsyncClient (parity bug), 2) our docs default to keepalive disabled via `trust_env=True` carryover on some images which sets shorter keepalive on certain platforms.

meera: parity is a blocker. we have async-heavy code paths that can't tune connections.

dev-bot: created issue redwood/devex#1902 (sdk-parity: async-client-missing-pool-limits)

meera: also timezone-y: when keepalive is low, nginx upstream closes idle connections and we see ECONNRESET which triggers retries and transient latency spikes.

jon: suggested fixes: - add max_connections and keepalive args to AsyncClient ctor (mirror sync) - add clear docs about trust_env and platform keepalive defaults - detect too-many-sockets and log a warning with `ulimit -n` hint

ravi: small UX tweak: make typing nicer. `PoolLimits` currently leaks httpx import in our top-level types; folks importing from redwood must `from httpx import Limits` which is annoying. propose we expose a thin redwood.types.PoolLimits alias.

meera: agree. also add runtime debug flag `REDWOOD_CLIENT_DUMP_SOCKETS=1` to dump socket counts to logs for 10s when set. helps ops.

jon: for immediate mitigation, ops increased node ephemeral ports and lowered TIME_WAIT recycle via sysctl, and added a restart cron for affected pods. not ideal.

ravi: will open PR to: (a) add pool args to AsyncClient with typing, (b) export a PoolLimits wrapper type, (c) update docs and an example snippet, (d) add an integ test that runs 100 QPS for 2m and asserts connection reuse ratio > 80%.

dev-bot: PR #1910 opened by ravi: feat(async): async client pool/keepalive parity + types export

meera: can you also add a note about retry/backoff interaction? currently backoff sleeps between retries create new connections on each attempt because the underlying transport is re-created in one internal code path. that was a surprise to me.

ravi: good catch. i'll audit places where transport is re-instantiated on retry and try to reuse transport across retry attempts.

jon: timeline: if tests pass we'll try a canary rollout mid-week. if it helps ops can apply the PoolLimits wrapper as a temporary patch in deployment configs.

meera: thanks — also small pedantic typing request: AsyncClient.__aenter__/__aexit__ signatures should include Coroutine[Any, Any, Optional["AsyncClient"]] or similar so contextmanager typing doesn't warn. tiny but reduces noise for strict mypy setups.

ravi: will include type fixes.

dev-bot: linked issues: redwood/devex#1902 -> PR #1910 -> changelog entry pending

meera: great. thanks team. we'll re-run load tomorrow and watch the socket metrics closely.
